plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win), so the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, and I pay less than my value in that case, maximizing expected profit. There's no benefit to bidding higher or lower than my true valuation of $13.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid regardless of my own bid, so bidding above my value risks losses, and bidding below reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and standard auction theory confirming truthful bidding is optimal, I will bid exactly my value of $15.

This is a second-price auction format where I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. The dominant strategy in this type of auction is to bid exactly my true value, since my bid only determines whether I win, not what I pay. Bidding my true value of $47 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (when others bid less) and avoid losing money (when others bid more than my value).
